section_summary: This section (pages 401–458) documents investigations by the Department of State, the Office of Naval Intelligence, and the Federal Communications Commission into reported Japanese interference with American shortwave broadcasts and radio circuits in the Far East. The correspondence details listener reports alleging deliberate mechanical jamming of English-language news broadcasts from General Electric international shortwave station W6XBE (later KGEI) in San Francisco, alongside inquiries conducted through U.S. diplomatic missions in Tokyo, Shanghai, Chungking, Peiping, and Batavia. It also records diplomatic and technical negotiations with the Japanese Department of Communications to eliminate second-harmonic interference emitted by station JDK against Press Wireless station KJY and reception in Manila.

subfiles.about: Forwarding correspondence concerning foreign interference with American radio news broadcasts for the State Department's confidential information.
subfiles.summary: Commander Nixon forwards correspondence indicating foreign interference with American radio news broadcasts, requesting confidential handling and their return.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Commander E. B. Nixon to Fletcher Warren Regarding Foreign Interference with American Radio News Broadcasts

subfiles.about: Transmitting letters received from the General Electric Company regarding radio broadcast interference.
subfiles.summary: Commander Connor forwards letters received from General Electric regarding radio interference, requesting their return after use.
subfiles.title: Letter from Commander F. W. Connor to Commander E. B. Nixon Forwarding Correspondence from General Electric Company

subfiles.about: Reporting deliberate Japanese interference with General Electric shortwave broadcasts to the Far East.
subfiles.summary: Harris reports deliberate Japanese interference with W6XBE English news broadcasts and explains bi-directional beam transmissions to Shanghai.
subfiles.title: Letter from E. T. B. Harris to Commander F. W. Connor Regarding Japanese Interference with Station W6XBE

subfiles.about: Reporting successful reception of W6XBE broadcasts in Hong Kong and suspected interference during news about Japan, Berlin, and Italy.
subfiles.summary: Rev. Burnside reports excellent reception of W6XBE in Hong Kong, noting suspected interference during broadcasts on Japan, Berlin, and Italy.
subfiles.title: Letter from Rev. W. M. Burnside to Short-Wave Station W6XBE on Radio Reception in Hong Kong

subfiles.about: Reporting intentional Japanese interference cutting into news broadcasts in British North Borneo.
subfiles.summary: Goldsborough reports from British North Borneo that Japanese radio interference appears deliberate because it only affects news broadcasts.
subfiles.title: Letter from E. Goldsborough to Radio Station W6XBE Concerning Intentional Japanese Radio Interference

subfiles.about: Submitting reception reports and logs for W6XBE broadcasts across the Pacific between Seattle, Japan, Shanghai, and Hong Kong.
subfiles.summary: Radio operator Sheil provides W6XBE reception logs from steamship Ixion, noting deliberate low-power Japanese squeals on English-language broadcasts.
subfiles.title: Letter and Reception Report from J. Sheil to Station W6XBE

subfiles.about: Commending W6XBE broadcasts received in Tokyo and suspecting intentional Japanese interference during evening news programs.
subfiles.summary: Mrs. Williams praises W6XBE morning reception in Tokyo, suggests English translations for Spanish broadcasts, and suspects intentional Japanese jamming of evening news.
subfiles.title: Letter from Mrs. Frank S. Williams to Radio Station W6XBE on Reception in Tokyo and Suspected Japanese Jamming

subfiles.about: Incomplete copy of letter reporting mechanical radio interference affecting W6XBE broadcasts in Medan, Sumatra.
subfiles.summary: Incomplete fragment of a letter describing mechanical interference superimposed on shortwave radio broadcasts from station W6XBE in Sumatra.
subfiles.title: Letter Fragment from A. L. Blume to Station W6XBE Regarding Mechanical Radio Interference in Sumatra

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of J. Sheil's reception report and log aboard T.S.S. Ixion.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of radio operator Sheil's report and log documenting W6XBE signal quality and Japanese interference across Pacific ports.
subfiles.title: Letter and Reception Report from J. Sheil to Station W6XBE (Duplicate Copy)

subfiles.about: Retained file copy of Commander Connor's letter forwarding General Electric radio interference reports.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate file copy of Commander Connor's letter transmitting General Electric correspondence concerning radio interference to Commander Nixon.
subfiles.title: Letter from Commander F. W. Connor to Commander E. B. Nixon Forwarding General Electric Letters (Duplicate Copy)

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of Harris's letter forwarding reports of deliberate Japanese interference with station W6XBE.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate file copy of Harris's letter forwarding reports of deliberate Japanese interference with station W6XBE English news broadcasts.
subfiles.title: Letter from E. T. B. Harris to Commander F. W. Connor Regarding Japanese Interference (Duplicate Copy)

subfiles.about: Retained copy of Rev. Burnside's letter reporting reception and suspected interference in Hong Kong.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of Rev. Burnside's letter reporting reception of W6XBE broadcasts and suspected censorship interference in Hong Kong.
subfiles.title: Letter from Rev. W. M. Burnside to Station W6XBE (Duplicate Copy)

subfiles.about: Complete duplicate copy of Mrs. Williams' letter concerning radio reception in Tokyo, censorship, and suspected Japanese jamming.
subfiles.summary: Complete duplicate copy of Mrs. Williams' letter reporting on W6XBE reception in Tokyo and suspecting intentional Japanese interference with news broadcasts.
subfiles.title: Letter from Mrs. Frank S. Williams to Station W6XBE on Reception in Tokyo (Duplicate Copy)

subfiles.about: Reporting on mechanical radio interference in Sumatra and offering constructive criticism on announcer pronunciation.
subfiles.summary: Blume reports intermittent mechanical interference affecting W6XBE in Sumatra and offers constructive criticism regarding the alternate announcer's English pronunciation.
subfiles.title: Letter from A. L. Blume to Station W6XBE on Radio Reception and Pronunciation

subfiles.about: Acknowledging receipt of naval intelligence memorandum and returning enclosed correspondence on radio interference.
subfiles.summary: Fletcher Warren acknowledges Commander Nixon's confidential memorandum on foreign radio interference and returns all enclosed correspondence as requested.
subfiles.title: Letter from Fletcher Warren to Commander E. B. Nixon Returning Enclosures

subfiles.about: Instructing the Tokyo Embassy to bring complaints of deliberate Japanese radio interference against General Electric stations to Japanese authorities.
subfiles.summary: Secretary Hull instructs the Tokyo Embassy to urge Japanese authorities to eliminate mechanical interference affecting General Electric shortwave broadcasts.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 217 from Secretary of State Hull to American Embassy Tokyo on Radio Interference Complaints

subfiles.about: Reporting that shortwave sets in Japan are restricted to diplomats who report no interference, and substantial proof is required before approaching Japanese authorities.
subfiles.summary: Dooman reports diplomats in Japan experience no radio interference and advises substantial proof is needed before approaching Japanese authorities.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 362 from Eugene H. Dooman to Secretary of State on Shortwave Licensing and Lack of Proof

subfiles.about: Departmental routing slip regarding radio communications correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Departmental routing slip from the Division of International Communications containing brief administrative annotations.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip from Division of International Communications

subfiles.about: Informal note regarding communications between Commander Nixon and naval authorities in China.
subfiles.summary: Informal handwritten departmental note commenting on Commander Nixon communicating directly with naval representatives in China.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Slip from Assistant Secretary's Office Regarding Commander Nixon

subfiles.about: Concurring with proposed action on radio interference and criticizing inappropriate remarks made by Mrs. Frank S. Williams in her letter.
subfiles.summary: FE concurs with investigating W6XBE interference, but objects to remarks by Mrs. Williams, suggesting an instruction to Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Division of Far Eastern Affairs on Interference and Mrs. Frank S. Williams' Letter

subfiles.about: Informing Commander Nixon of Tokyo's response regarding radio interference and stating that Embassy Chungking is seeking specific evidence.
subfiles.summary: Warren informs Commander Nixon of Tokyo's report that diplomats experience no interference, notes substantial evidence is required for protests, and states Chungking is investigating.
subfiles.title: Letter from Fletcher Warren to Commander E. B. Nixon Regarding Tokyo Embassy Report and China Inquiries

subfiles.about: Departmental carbon copy of Fletcher Warren's letter to Commander Nixon regarding radio interference investigations.
subfiles.summary: Carbon copy of letter to Commander Nixon regarding Tokyo Embassy findings and investigations in Chungking concerning Japanese radio interference.
subfiles.title: Letter from Fletcher Warren to Commander E. B. Nixon (Carbon Copy)

subfiles.about: Additional departmental copy of letter to Commander Nixon regarding alleged Japanese radio interference.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate file copy of letter to Commander Nixon reviewing diplomatic reports on shortwave reception in Japan and China.
subfiles.title: Letter from Fletcher Warren to Commander E. B. Nixon (File Copy)

subfiles.about: Additional file copy of letter informing Commander Nixon of radio interference inquiries in the Far East.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate file copy of Warren's letter to Nixon concerning radio reception reports from Tokyo and inquiries through Chungking.
subfiles.title: Letter from Fletcher Warren to Commander E. B. Nixon (Duplicate Copy)

subfiles.about: Analyzing Tokyo's telegram on radio interference and recommending inquiries through the American Embassy in China.
subfiles.summary: Otterman recommends informing the Navy Department that tangible proof of Japanese interference is required and suggests sending a telegram to Embassy Chungking to gather evidence.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Harvey B. Otterman to Fletcher Warren Regarding Tokyo Telegram on Radio Interference

subfiles.about: Instructing the Chungking Embassy to investigate alleged Japanese interference with General Electric shortwave broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary Welles instructs Embassy Chungking to ascertain the extent and obtain concrete evidence of Japanese interference with W6XBE/KGEI broadcasts.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 157 from Acting Secretary of State Welles to American Embassy Chungking on Radio Interference Inquiries

subfiles.about: Reporting that Japanese authorities are preparing a report on Press Wireless interference and inquiring whether interference has ceased.
subfiles.summary: Dooman reports the Japanese Department of Communications is preparing a report on Press Wireless interference and asks whether interference has ceased.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 413 from Eugene H. Dooman to Secretary of State on Press Wireless Interference

subfiles.about: Forwarding Tokyo telegram regarding Japanese station JDK interference with Press Wireless station KJY.
subfiles.summary: Messersmith transmits Tokyo telegram No. 413 to the FCC, requesting confirmation on whether station JDK interference with station KJY has ceased.
subfiles.title: Letter from Assistant Secretary of State Messersmith to Frank R. McNinch Transmitting Tokyo Telegram

subfiles.about: Transmitting the Japanese Department of Communications' finding that station JDK's harmonic emission is negligible and requesting technical measurement data.
subfiles.summary: Dooman transmits Japan's reply that JDK's second harmonic is under 0.5 watt, requesting interference measurements and technical details.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 436 from Eugene H. Dooman to Secretary of State Transmitting Japanese Communications Reply

subfiles.about: Forwarding Japanese report on station JDK second harmonic and requesting technical information from the FCC.
subfiles.summary: Messersmith transmits Tokyo telegram No. 436 containing the Japanese communications report, inviting the FCC to supply requested technical information regarding JDK interference.
subfiles.title: Letter from Assistant Secretary Messersmith to Frank R. McNinch Transmitting Japanese Communications Report

subfiles.about: Reporting that Press Wireless advised interference from Japanese station JDK continues daily between 0000 and 0400 GMT.
subfiles.summary: McNinch informs the Secretary of State that Press Wireless reported continued daily interference to Station KJY from Japanese station JDK.
subfiles.title: Letter from Frank R. McNinch to Secretary of State on Continued Interference to Station KJY

subfiles.about: Reporting results of consultations with local officials and listeners in Shanghai regarding interference with KGEI and W6XBE broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: Consul General Gauss reports consultations with military, police, commercial, and amateur radio sources in Shanghai; interference with KGEI was irregular and not conclusively deliberate jamming.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 778 from Clarence E. Gauss to Secretary of State on Radio Interference Inquiries in Shanghai

subfiles.about: Instructing the Shanghai consulate to forward mail copies of telegrams regarding radio interference to the Tokyo Embassy.
subfiles.summary: Secretary Hull instructs the Shanghai consulate to mail code texts of interference telegrams to the Tokyo Embassy for information.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 333 from Secretary of State Hull to American Consul Shanghai on Forwarding Telegrams to Tokyo

subfiles.about: Reporting radio reception monitoring of KGEI in Chungking and finding no deliberate interference.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Johnson reports monitoring in Chungking detected no deliberate interference with KGEI, though heterodyne interference from station ZBW Hong Kong occurred.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 516 from Nelson T. Johnson to Secretary of State on Radio Monitoring in Chungking

subfiles.about: Agreeing to obtain technical information from Press Wireless and monitor Japanese station JDK.
subfiles.summary: Chairman McNinch confirms the FCC will obtain additional data from Press Wireless and monitor Japanese station JDK.
subfiles.title: Letter from Frank R. McNinch to Secretary of State Regarding FCC Monitoring of Station JDK

subfiles.about: Instructing the Batavia consulate to investigate reported radio interference with W6XBE/KGEI broadcasts in Java.
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary Moore informs the Batavia consulate of Consul Clattenburg's report of interference in Java and requests an investigation into possible Japanese involvement.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Acting Secretary of State Moore to American Consul Batavia on Radio Interference in Java

subfiles.about: Reporting that mechanical interference with KGEI is not evident in Java and noting previous Morse code interference has ceased.
subfiles.summary: Consul General Dickover reports mechanical interference is not evident in Java, noting weak signals and Morse transmissions that have largely ceased.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 41 from Erle R. Dickover to Secretary of State on Radio Reception in Java

subfiles.about: Conveying Press Wireless's request that Japan install parallel tuned circuits on station JDK transmission lines to curb second harmonic radiation.
subfiles.summary: Chairman Fly conveys Press Wireless's request that Japan install parallel tuned circuits on station JDK transmission lines to curb harmonic radiation.
subfiles.title: Letter from James Lawrence Fly to Secretary of State Proposing Technical Remedy for Station JDK Interference

subfiles.about: Instructing the Tokyo Embassy to ask Japanese authorities to install parallel tuned circuits on station JDK to eliminate harmonic interference.
subfiles.summary: Secretary Hull instructs Embassy Tokyo to ask Japanese authorities to install a parallel tuned circuit on station JDK's transmission line.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 302 from Secretary of State Hull to American Embassy Tokyo on Technical Adjustment to Station JDK

subfiles.about: Informing the FCC that instructions have been telegraphed to Tokyo to request installation of tuned circuits on station JDK.
subfiles.summary: Messersmith informs Chairman Fly that the Tokyo Embassy was instructed to request the proposed technical remedy on Japanese station JDK.
subfiles.title: Letter from Assistant Secretary Messersmith to James Lawrence Fly Concerning Representations to Tokyo

subfiles.about: Reporting that a Japanese station broadcasting in English and Japanese completely blankets KGEI on the 31-meter band.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Johnson reports a Japanese station broadcasting in English and Japanese completely blankets KGEI on the 31-meter band.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 549 from Nelson T. Johnson to Secretary of State on Japanese Station Blanketing KGEI

subfiles.about: Reporting identification of Japanese interfering stations JZJ, JZK, and JZI and Japanese claims regarding frequencies.
subfiles.summary: Consul General Gauss reports Shanghai observers identified interfering Japanese stations JZJ, JZK, and JZI, whose spokesman suggested Americans change wavelengths.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 897 from Clarence E. Gauss to Secretary of State Identifying Japanese Stations JZJ, JZK, and JZI

subfiles.about: Reporting Consul Clattenburg's information on radio interference in Java and recommending inquiries through Consul General Dickover.
subfiles.summary: Otterman recommends investigating reported radio interference in Java through Consul General Dickover to obtain evidence for representations against Japan.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Harvey B. Otterman to Thomas Burke on Radio Interference in Java

subfiles.about: Requesting Ambassador Grew to ensure Mrs. Frank S. Williams does not communicate with station W6XBE to protect the Navy's confidential status.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck requests Ambassador Grew to caution Mr. Williams that his wife must not contact the radio station, protecting confidential naval sources.
subfiles.title: Letter to Ambassador Joseph C. Grew Regarding Mrs. Frank S. Williams' Letter and Source Protection

subfiles.about: Reporting Japanese station JZI ceased interference after publicity and advising that KGEI is sandwiched between Hong Kong and Berlin stations.
subfiles.summary: Lockhart reports station JZI ceased interference, recommends withholding representations, and notes KGEI is sandwiched between Hong Kong and Berlin stations.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 533 from Frank P. Lockhart to Secretary of State Regarding Japanese Station JZI and Frequency Congestion

subfiles.about: Explaining that the reply to Peiping's telegram is postponed pending redrafting and receipt of a new telegram from Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Saugstad notes reply to Peiping telegram No. 533 is postponed to redraft a conflicting telegram and await Tokyo reports.
subfiles.title: File Memorandum from Division of International Communications on Postponing Reply to Peiping Telegram
